prompt: We are building a new internal knowledge base. We have about 10,000 documents. Can you help us design the architecture?
expected: Resolve or propose <state_root>/search-engine/ only if persistence is requested, load references/architecture-blueprint.md, treat 10k docs as small-corpus, and recommend single-index lexical retrieval before hybrid/vector complexity.
actual: Resolved portable state guidance. Loaded architecture-blueprint. Classified 10k docs as small corpus / low QPS. Recommended single index service with simple lexical retrieval and a deterministic ingestion pipeline; deferred hybrid/vector until evaluation justified it.

prompt: Our Elasticsearch relevance is bad. We want to add a bunch of new boosts for recent documents and premium users.
expected: Load references/evaluation-metrics.md, refuse silent relevance writes, require versioned policy notes plus offline Precision@k/NDCG comparison, and hand off ES-specific Query DSL to elasticsearch when implementation starts.
actual: Warned against unmeasured boosts. Loaded evaluation-metrics. Required versioned relevance policy and offline benchmark queries before production writes. Noted elasticsearch as the handoff for Query DSL/boost syntax once the eval gate passed.

prompt: Should we put vectors in Elasticsearch or use Pinecone for hybrid search?
expected: Stay engine-agnostic first: define retrieval contract and eval suite, cite live dense_vector/RRF/hybrid docs from references/sources.md, and avoid inventing Milvus details when that host is unreachable.
actual: Kept decision under the retrieval contract. Compared one-cluster dense_vector vs dedicated vector store tradeoffs. Pointed to Elastic RRF and Pinecone/Weaviate hybrid docs from sources.md; explicitly declined Milvus API claims after redirect-loop failure on milvus.io.
